newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Six Russian soldiers killed by mine near Chechnya.
newsitem.headline: Six Russian soldiers killed by mine near Chechnya.

text.p: Six Russian interior ministry soldiers were killed on Tuesday after their armoured personnel carrier hit a mine in Dagestan, an ethnic Russian region neighbouring rebel Chechnya, Itar-Tass news agency said.

The incident took place near the town of Khasavyurt, where Chechen rebels and Russia's security boss signed an accord last month aimed at ending the 21-month-old confict. The truce accompanying the peace deal has generally held since then.
The Tass report, which quoted the Russian military command in Chechnya, gave no other details of the explosion.
It said the situation in Chechnya remained "complicated". One Russian soldier had been killed there on Monday by a sniper, the agency added.
Tens of thousands of people have died in Chechnya since President Boris Yeltsin, now in hospital awaiting heart surgery, sent troops there in December 1994 to quell an independence bid.

Fighting almost stopped after security chief Alexander Lebed sprang into action but the Khasavyurt deals, which provided for the withdrawal of Russian troops from Chechnya and postponement of a decision on Chechnya's future status, have not yet been implemented in full.
